key_insight: Adapting both model choice and stopping to observed outputs and server congestion minimizes the modeled long-run cost of classification errors, queries, and waiting.
engineering_relevance: Shared LLM classification services can use congestion prices to balance accuracy gains against query fees and system-wide delays.
method: Represent adaptive routing policies as mixtures of decision trees and optimize model loads via convex optimization.
Use a Bayesian dynamic program with marginal congestion prices to select models and decide when to stop.
Compute policies through column generation with an explicit optimality-gap bound.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments separating the benefits of adaptive model selection and congestion awareness, but gives no datasets or quantitative results.
watch_item: Exact holding-cost formulas assume specific queueing models; deployment requires checking how well these assumptions match actual LLM serving behavior.
paper_title: Congestion-Aware Adaptive Routing for LLM Classification
